Fit a rating from evidence

Source: R/fit_rating.R
fit_rating.Rd

The guided way to a rating. Give it evidence and it fits one, with defaults chosen so that a careful analyst would not argue, and it records what it did. An expert who wants more control can still call rate_optimise() or rate_optimise_segmented() directly; this function calls them.

What it decides for you, and where to change it:

  • One limb. A single equation \(Q = C(H - a)^n\) across the whole range, unless you supply controls (breakpoint stages) or ask for limbs = "suggest". A rating with several limbs is a modelling decision and is never made silently.

  • Suggested breakpoints are advisory. With limbs = "suggest" the function uses suggest_breakpoints(), records that the breakpoints came from a statistical search and not from field evidence, and says so each time the rating is printed. They are candidates for a person to review. Breakpoints you give in controls are recorded with the origin you state in breakpoint_origin ("user_judgement" if you do not), so a reviewer can tell a surveyed change of control from a better AIC. See breakpoint_origins().

  • The relative objective. Gauging error is typically proportional to the reading, so the fit minimises error in log discharge. Use objective = "absolute" for rate_optimise()'s own default. See vignette("mathematical_contract") for both.

  • What is used. Rows marked included = FALSE, rows with a missing or non-finite stage or discharge, negative discharge, and (for the relative objective) zero discharge are not used. Each is listed with its reason in the rating's provenance, and none is deleted from your evidence.

  • Where it may be applied. A rating made here can be applied only within the stage range it was gauged over until you state the range it may be used over, with operational_limits or set_operational_limits(). That states the decision, and its basis, to use the rating there.

The rating stores the call, the seed, every starting point tried, and the evidence it used with each row's evidence_id, so it can be reproduced and checked.

Usage

fit_rating(
  evidence,
  controls = NULL,
  breakpoint_origin = "user_judgement",
  limbs = c("one", "suggest"),
  model = c("independent", "segmented"),
  objective = c("relative", "absolute"),
  age_halflife = NULL,
  age_min_weight = 0.1,
  reference_time = NULL,
  protect_above = NULL,
  protect_quantile = NULL,
  protect_width = 0.05,
  n_boot = 0L,
  seed = NULL,
  operational_limits = NULL,
  operational_basis = NA_character_,
  quiet = FALSE
)

Arguments

evidence

A FlodeEvidence, or a data.frame or data.table that as_flode_evidence() accepts, including the table read_gaugings() returns.

controls

Numeric vector of breakpoint stages, or NULL (default) for one limb. Each must lie inside the stage range of the evidence used.

breakpoint_origin

Where the breakpoints in controls came from: one value from breakpoint_origins() for all of them, or one per breakpoint. Default "user_judgement". Ignored for limbs = "suggest", whose breakpoints are always "statistical_candidate".

limbs

"one" (default) or "suggest". "suggest" finds breakpoints with suggest_breakpoints() and uses those it selects, marked as advisory. Not allowed together with controls.

model

"independent" (default) fits each limb separately with rate_optimise(). "segmented" fits one joint equation with rate_optimise_segmented().

objective

"relative" (default) or "absolute".

age_halflife, age_min_weight, reference_time

Optional recency weighting, as in rate_optimise(): a half-life in days, the weight floor, and the time ages are measured from (NULL is the latest gauging). Needs an observation_time on every row used.

protect_above, protect_quantile, protect_width

Optional magnitude protection for recency weighting, as in rate_optimise(): gaugings at or above a discharge (protect_above, m3/s) or a quantile of the gauged discharges (protect_quantile) keep their full weight however old they are. Needs age_halflife. The threshold is recorded in the provenance.

n_boot

Number of bootstrap refits per limb for coefficient uncertainty. Default 0. Only for model = "independent".

seed

Integer or NULL. Used for the bootstrap, and recorded so a fit can be repeated.

operational_limits

NULL (default) or c(lower, upper): the stage range, in metres, over which the rating may be applied.

operational_basis

Character. Why that range: for example the gauged range, a structure's limit, or a review decision.

quiet

Logical. TRUE suppresses the summary message.

Value

A FlodeRating (or FlodeSegmentedRating for model = "segmented") whose @gaugings is the evidence that was used, with each row's evidence_id, and whose provenance records the call, seed, exclusions, breakpoint origin and operational limits (read it with rating_provenance()). Its lifecycle is "draft".

See also

read_gaugings(), validate_gaugings(), set_operational_limits(), rate_optimise(), rating_provenance()

Examples

set.seed(1)
gaugings <- data.frame(stage_m = round(seq(0.4, 3, length.out = 20), 3))
gaugings$discharge_cms <- round(3.2 * gaugings$stage_m^1.6 * exp(rnorm(20, sd = 0.03)), 3)
fit <- fit_rating(gaugings)
#> fit_rating(): 20 of 20 rows used; relative objective, independent model, one limb.
#>   No operational limits set: stages beyond the gauged range are returned and flagged as extrapolation. See set_operational_limits().
fit
#> <FlodeRating> 1 limb(s), origin: independently_fitted, lifecycle: draft
#>   converged: yes (1 of 1 limb)
#>   valid: yes
#>   breakpoints: one limb
#>   evidence: 20 of 20 rows used
#>   operational limits: not set; stages beyond the gauged range 0.4 to 3 m are flagged as extrapolation
#>     limb lower_stage_m upper_stage_m        C          a        n  rmse_cms
#>    <int>         <num>         <num>    <num>      <num>    <num>     <num>
#> 1:     1           0.4             3 3.286169 0.01254205 1.588275 0.2498467
#>    r_squared
#>        <num>
#> 1: 0.9980051

# The rating can be applied within the range it was gauged over.
apply_rating(fit, c(0.8, 1.5, 2.5))
#>    stage discharge extrapolated                support
#>    <num>     <num>       <lgcl>                 <char>
#> 1:   0.8  2.248384        FALSE interpolation_observed
#> 2:   1.5  6.174183        FALSE interpolation_observed
#> 3:   2.5 13.972011        FALSE interpolation_observed

# To apply it more widely, state the range and why.
wider <- set_operational_limits(fit, 0.2, 3.5, basis = "channel control confirmed to 3.5 m")
apply_rating(wider, c(0.3, 3.4))
#> INFO [2026-11-27 07:00:56] apply_rating(): 2 of 2 stage value(s) fell outside the rating and were extrapolated.
#>    stage  discharge extrapolated       support
#>    <num>      <num>       <lgcl>        <char>
#> 1:   0.3  0.4536877         TRUE extrapolation
#> 2:   3.4 22.8178884         TRUE extrapolation

# What the fit recorded.
str(rating_provenance(fit)$fit_rating[c("call", "model", "objective", "n_used")])
#> List of 4
#>  $ call     : chr "fit_rating(evidence = gaugings)"
#>  $ model    : chr "independent"
#>  $ objective: chr "relative"
#>  $ n_used   : int 20
